mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the FEDFUNDS rate increased by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% in a month indicates a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where HOUST dropped by more than 5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month indicates a surge in economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where INDPRO increased by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate revenues and profits grow.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods where RSAFS showed a sustained increase over three months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) coupled with an increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month indicates a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending rise.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decrease & PAYEMS increase > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where UNRATE decreased and PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) coupled with a rise in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.3% in a month signals inflationary pressure with accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate higher nominal earnings.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decrease & CPIAUCSL increase > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS decreased and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.3% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and economic outlook improve.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the periods where GDPC1 showed a sustained increase over two consecutive quarters.
